parts.title: Session twenty, and this agent still starts from zero.
parts.headline: The same context. Rebuilt again.
spoken: Session twenty, and this agent still starts from zero.
Each new session has to piece its context together.
The counter rises. What it retains stays at zero.
What could the next session read before it starts?
Give it shared instructions, a knowledge index, and a record of decisions.
Then it starts from what's already been checked, and leaves something useful behind.

excerpt.text: Write docs/workspace-layout.md with a table of path, job and writer

parts.next: Next: can your next agent check what this one found?

parts.title: Can your next agent check what this one found?
parts.headline: The chat closes. The evidence stays.
spoken: Can your next agent check what this one found?
Findings can get buried in chat history.
Give it a filesystem and a shell.
Now it can open the file, run the test, and leave a record.
A claim can point to a file. A fix, to a test and its result.
So the next agent can find it, and check it.

excerpt.text: Cite each claim as path:line or as the command you ran.

parts.title: Can your agent find the right check before it finishes?
parts.headline: One route. One check.
spoken: Can your agent find the right check before it finishes?
Start with AGENTS.md: a short table of when, and what to read.
Changing tests? The table routes the agent to the testing doc.
Read top-down before writing. Write evidence back as you work.
Then it runs the check the primer names, before calling the work done.

excerpt.text: Draft AGENTS.md for this repository as a routing primer, under 300 lines.

parts.title: Can you change agent tools without rebuilding an integration?
parts.headline: Change the agent. Keep the integration?
spoken: Can you change agent tools without rebuilding an integration?
The harness is the loop making model and tool calls.
Keep the integration outside that loop.
Put it behind a CLI or an MCP server, where that boundary makes sense.
Then changing harnesses need not mean rebuilding every capability.

excerpt.text: say whether the same capability could live behind an MCP server or a CLI that any harness can call

parts.next: Next: where did this answer come from?

parts.title: Can you trace this agent result back to its source?
parts.headline: Where did this answer come from?
spoken: Can you trace this agent result back to its source?
Keep three folders.
Bronze holds the source. Silver holds what was extracted. Gold holds the accepted result.
Your agent can search, read, and compare these files.
Keep links between them, so a result can be traced back to its inputs.

excerpt.text: silver: typed records citing file, page and span in bronze
